steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Legal evaluation requires assessing the strengths and weaknesses of a law, principle or proposal and reaching a supported judgement

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: A balanced argument presents points on both sides — for and against — before reaching a conclusion; one-sided answers cannot access top mark bands

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Always support your points with specific legal examples, cases or statistics — vague or generalised statements score poorly

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: When evaluating a legal rule, consider: how effectively it achieves its purpose, whether it is clear and certain, whether it is fair and just, and whether there are gaps or inconsistencies

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Q: What does a balanced evaluation require? | Q: How do you evaluate the effectiveness of a legal rule? | Q: Why is it important to consider the law in practice as well as the law on the books?

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always signpost your evaluation: 'A significant strength is...', 'However, a key weakness is...', 'On balance...' Use the PEEL structure for paragraphs: Point, Evidence (legal example), Explanation, Link back to the question Don't sit on the fence — reach a clear judgement, but make sure it is supported by your analysis Include at least one specific case or statute in each paragraph — this demonstrates legal knowledge and supports your evaluation Practise writing conclusions that summarise the key reasons for your judgement in two to three sentences
